page: Microsoft Azure E32-16as_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked at up to 4.5 GHz. Built on x86_64 architecture and managed via Microsoft Hyper-V, the system provides 16 dedicated virtual CPUs across 8 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The CPU configuration includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, alongside instruction set support for AVX-512, AVX-VNNI, and cryptographic extensions like AES and SHA-NI.

A defining characteristic of the E32-16as_v7 is its substantial memory capacity of 256 GB, providing an allocation of 16 GB of RAM per virtual CPU. The instance does not include bundled local storage, relying on external Azure storage options for non-volatile persistence, and is provisioned without complimentary public IPv4 addresses or hardware GPU accelerators. Memory benchmarks demonstrate 51.68 GB/sec read and 34.29 GB/sec write throughput for large uncached transfers.

Benchmark results highlight strong single-threaded processing capabilities. The instance scores in the top tier for single-core stress-ng tests, single-threaded gzip compression, bzip3 decompression, and Geekbench single-core evaluations. Multi-threaded metrics, including Geekbench multi-core and stress-ng multi-core tests, align within mid-tier percentiles, reflecting the constrained 16-vCPU footprint against higher core-count configurations.

The constrained core count paired with massive memory capacity offers distinct cost efficiency for workloads constrained by licensing fees tied to core counts while demanding significant RAM. The E32-16as_v7 is suited for in-memory databases, large-footprint caching platforms such as Redis, enterprise memory-bound data processing pipelines, and lightweight CPU-based language model inference.
description: Microsoft Azure E32-16as_v7 is a memory-optimized instance featuring 16 dedicated vCPUs derived from 8 physical cores on an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor running at 4.5 GHz. Built on x86_64 architecture with Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance incorporates AVX-512 vector support and provides 256 GB of system RAM, yielding a high ratio of 16 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include local disk storage or GPU accelerators, relying on remote network-attached block storage for persistence. Benchmark results show top-tier single-core CPU throughput alongside average multi-core metrics, reflecting its 16-vCPU boundary. With 51.68 GB/sec read memory bandwidth and solid single-thread performance, this configuration is cost-effective for core-licensed environments requiring extensive memory, including large-scale in-memory caching systems, transactional databases, and memory-intensive analytics workloads.
